# CLI Reference Manual (`informal`)

Complete command-line interface reference generated directly from `crates/informal-cli/src/main.rs`.

## Synopsis

```sh
informal [GLOBAL OPTIONS] <COMMAND> [ARGS]
```

## Global Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--mem-gb <MEM_GB>` | Memory budget for in-process engines, in GB (0 = none). Default: 90% of the cgroup's memory.max (or memory.high) when it has one, else 75% of physical memory. Over it, they stop with unknown "memory"; 10% over it (or near the cgroup limit), informal exits with a memout (status 3) |
| `--isolate` | Run each in-house engine in a process of its own (also with the environment variable INFORMAL_ISOLATE): an engine that runs out of memory or crashes ends alone. Each then loads the model itself |
| `-h, --help` | Print help information |
| `-V, --version` | Print version information |

## Subcommands Summary

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`informal info`](#informal-info) | Parse and validate a Btor2 model and print its features as JSON |
| [`informal fmt`](#informal-fmt) | Print a Btor2 model in canonical form |
| [`informal check`](#informal-check) | Check one model with the engine portfolio |
| [`informal simp`](#informal-simp) | Load a model at bit level (AIGER, or Btor2 bit-blasted), preprocess it and print its size before and after; `--aag` prints the result |

| [`informal reduce`](#informal-reduce) | Shrink an AIGER model while two engines keep disagreeing on it, or while a test command keeps exiting 0 (delta debugging) |
| [`informal split`](#informal-split) | Prove a property whose bad output is an OR of several terms part by part: one model per term, proved a few at a time with the invariant store carrying each certified invariant to the others, then the original with all of them (see docs/engines.md) |
| [`informal bench`](#informal-bench) | Run engines over every model in a directory and log to the run database |
| [`informal docgen`](#informal-docgen) | Generate or verify single-source-of-truth Markdown reference manuals, `docs/reference/index.json`, and `llms.txt` from CLI, Tcl, and MCP registries |

## Exit Codes

| Context | Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `informal check` | `10` | **UNSAFE** — counterexample found and replayed |
| `informal check` | `20` | **SAFE** — unbounded proof verified |
| `informal check` | `0` | **UNKNOWN** — timeout or inconclusive |
| `informal shell --check` | `0` | Script clean (only honoured or ignored vendor options) |
| `informal shell --check` | `1` | Script has rejected options, unknown commands, or Tcl errors |
| Any command | `3` | Memory budget exceeded (`--mem-gb` or cgroup limit) |
| Any command | `1` / `2` | Runtime error or CLI usage error |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `INFORMAL_ISOLATE` | Run each in-house engine in an isolated child process (equivalent to `--isolate`) |
| `INFORMAL_WAVE_VIEWER` | Waveform viewer spawned by Tcl `visualize` (e.g., `surfer`, `gtkwave`) |
| `INFORMAL_AI_SOCKET` | Override desktop app Unix socket path, or `off` to disable AI socket |
| `INFORMAL_AI_MODE` | Desktop app MCP permission mode (`read-only`, `propose`, `auto`) |
| `INFORMAL_ROOT` | Default workspace root passed by the Antigravity MCP launcher |
| `INFORMAL_TOOLS_DIR` | Build/runtime directory for external solvers (`cadical`, `bitwuzla`) |
| `INFORMAL_CADICAL_DIR` | Explicit CaDiCaL build directory override |
| `INFORMAL_BITWUZLA_DIR` | Explicit Bitwuzla install directory override |

```sh

```

| Argument / Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<MODEL>` | — |  |
| `--engines <ENGINES>` | `config/engines.toml` |  |
| `--timeout <TIMEOUT>` | `60` | Wall-clock budget in seconds |
| `--only <ONLY>` | — | Only use these engines (comma-separated names) |
| `--certificate <DIR>` | — | Write the verdict's certificate into this directory, for a checker that shares no code with InFormal: a counterexample as an AIGER witness (aigsim), a proof as a witness circuit (Certifaiger), and `<model>.cert.json`, which says what was written (see docs/certificates.md) |


### `informal shell`

Run a JasperGold or VC Formal style Tcl script (or an interactive shell when no script is given)

```sh
informal shell [script] [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument / Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SCRIPT>` | — |  |
| `--flavor <FLAVOR>` | — | Command set: jg or vcf (default: detected from the script) |
| `--engines <ENGINES>` | `config/engines.toml` |  |
| `--workdir <WORKDIR>` | `informal_work` | Scratch directory for generated models |
| `-c, --command <COMMANDS>` | — | Evaluate this Tcl before the script (repeatable) |
| `--check` | — | Check the script instead of running it: nothing is elaborated or proved; every command and option informal would reject, ignore or does not know is listed with its line. Exit status 1 when the script would not run to its end |
| `--json` | — | With --check: print the report as JSON |
| `--certificate <DIR>` | — | Write the certificate of every property the in-house engines settle into this directory, as `check --certificate` does for a model (docs/certificates.md) |

### `informal mcp`

Serve one FPV session to an AI model as Model Context Protocol tools on standard input and output (docs/ai-interface.md). Replies are JSON; what the session prints goes to standard error

```sh
informal mcp [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument / Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mode <MODE>` | `propose` | What the model may do: read-only (read and prove), propose (changes wait for a person) or auto (changes apply at once, tagged AI-added; for an evaluation sandbox) |
| `--root <ROOT>` | `.` | Scripts and design files are only opened below this directory |
| `--engines <ENGINES>` | `config/engines.toml` |  |
| `--workdir <WORKDIR>` | `informal_work` | Scratch directory for generated models and traces |
| `--max-time <MAX_TIME>` | `300` | The longest time limit, in seconds, a prove call may ask for |
| `--connect <SOCKET>` | — | Do not start a session: connect to the one a running desktop app serves and pass the messages through, so the model works on the session a person is looking at. Without a socket path, the most recently started app's. The app sets the mode; the other options are not used |

### `informal reduce`

Shrink an AIGER model while two engines keep disagreeing on it, or while a test command keeps exiting 0 (delta debugging)

```sh
informal reduce <model> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument / Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<MODEL>` | — |  |
| `--disagree <DISAGREE>` | — | Two engine names; the model is kept interesting while they give the same two conflicting definitive verdicts as on the original |
| `--test <TEST>` | — | A shell command run on each candidate; `{}` is replaced by the candidate's path (else the path is appended). Exit 0 = keep |
| `--engines <ENGINES>` | `config/engines.toml` |  |
| `--timeout <TIMEOUT>` | `10` | Seconds per engine run (with --disagree) |
| `-o, --out <OUT>` | `reduced.aag` | Where the reduced model is written (ASCII AIGER) |
| `--workdir <WORKDIR>` | `informal_work/reduce` | Scratch directory for candidates |

### `informal split`

Prove a property whose bad output is an OR of several terms part by part: one model per term, proved a few at a time with the invariant store carrying each certified invariant to the others, then the original with all of them (see docs/engines.md)

```sh
informal split <model> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument / Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<MODEL>` | — |  |
| `--timeout <TIMEOUT>` | `300` | Wall-clock budget in seconds, for the terms and the original |
| `--jobs <JOBS>` | `4` | Terms proved at once |
| `--max-terms <MAX_TERMS>` | `256` | Open OR nodes until there are this many terms |
| `--slice <SLICE>` | `10` | Seconds per term in the first round; doubles every round |
| `--workdir <WORKDIR>` | `informal_work/split` | Scratch directory for the term models and the private store |
| `--write-only` | — | Only write the term models (kept in the scratch directory) |
